items.title: Using children for election campaign in bad taste but not ground to invalidate election: Madras High Court
items.summary: The Madras High Court on Thursday held that the use of children for a political party's election campaigns is in bad taste, but such conduct, by itself, is not a ground to invalidate an election [ K Sivakumar v R Rajendran ]. Justice D Bharatha Chakravarthy criticised the use of children to influence their parents' voting choices through social media videos. However, the Court held that such persuasion could not automatically be treated as undue influence under the Representation of the People Act, 1951 (RP Act), to void an election. The Court added that it is up to lawmakers in Parliament to decide whether such practices should be banned or made a ground for setting aside an election. " The entire act of involving tender children is in bad taste, and the tasks they were allowed to perform reflect poor parenting; making reels out of it is cheap and politically motivated. This is a larger debate for the nation and Parliament to consider, including whether to prohibit it or make it grounds to set aside the election," the Court held. items.title: Lucio AI launches Legal Research Agent in Open Beta, offers 25 Free Searches
items.summary: Lucio AI has launched Lucio Research , a legal research agent released as an open beta through Lucio Labs. The tool searches, screens, reads and cites across hundreds of legal sources for each question. It is free to use for one month, with up to 25 searches per user. The launch addresses a familiar constraint in legal research. Much of the time spent on a research question goes into finding and screening material rather than analysing it and research usually ends when time runs out rather than when every relevant authority has been read. Lucio says the beta is designed to test how far that limit can be pushed. Lucio Research runs in two modes. According to the company, Standard mode runs a focused search of the core authorities and typically reviews 300 to 500 sources per question. In-depth mode explores about three times as many sources and checks for gaps, usually returning an answer in under three minutes. The company says it often reviews 800 to 1,500 sources in this mode and more than 2,000 on some questions. The programme was especially meant for girl students and young women to pursue leadership positions in judiciary, legal profession and academic institutions. The inaugural session began with welcome address by Vice-Chancellor (VC) Prof (Dr) Bindu S Ronald and setting of theme by Justice Abhay S Oka — former Judge of Supreme Court of India. Justice Oka said that women should not be counted only in numbers but also in terms of presence in positions of authority and decision making; women should be encouraged to go down the ladder from lower judiciary to higher judiciary, senior administrative and leadership positions in academic institutions etc.; create an environment where young girls can see themselves as judges, heads of institutions, legal scholars and decision makers. items.title: Was our order relied upon to de-notify Jantar Mantar as protest site? Supreme Court seeks Centre's response
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday asked for the Central government's response to a plea challenging the Union Home Ministry's de-notification of Delhi's Jantar Mantar as a protest site. Pertinently, the Delhi Police on October 13 told the Delhi High Court that the decision was taken based on the Supreme Court's order of October 9. However, the Central government today denied the same. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi questioned the Centre, "[Was it de-notified] Because of some oral observations of the Court, or was there an application of mind with regard to the site and its efficacy in being used as a common protest site?" CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Union, replied, "The Court's judgment is not the basis of the decision. The committee was constituted much before. The committee has given a detailed report." SG Tushar Mehta Senior Advocate Mukta Gupta , appearing for the petitioner, stressed on the fundamental rights of citizens to protest peacefully.
